items.title: [Serve] Allow app-defined health routes to bypass `max_ongoing_requests`
items.author: codechrl
items.body_excerpt:
### Description

Every request to a route on a `@serve.ingress` FastAPI app counts toward the deployment's `max_ongoing_requests`. A health route such as `GET /healthz` therefore waits for a free slot while the replicas are saturated. External health checkers (load balancers, Kubernetes probes) time out on it and mark a working application as down.

Repro on Ray 2.54.1 and FastAPI 0.116.0:

```python
import asyncio
import threading
import time

import requests
from fastapi import FastAPI
from ray import serve

app = FastAPI()


@serve.deployment(max_ongoing_requests=2)
@serve.ingress(app)
class Api:
    @app.get("/work")
    async def work(self):
        await asyncio.sleep(6)

    @app.get("/healthz")
    async def healthz(self):
        return "ok"


def timed_get(path):
    start = time.time()
    status = requests.get(f"http://127.0.0.1:8000{path}").status_code
    print(path, status, f"{time.time() - start:.2f}s")


serve.run(Api.bind())
timed_get("/healthz")

for _ in range(2):
    threading.Thread(target=timed_get, args=("/work",)).start()
time.sleep(1)
timed_get("/-/healthz")
timed_get("/healthz")
```

```text
/healthz 200 0.65s
/-/healthz 200 0.03s
/work 200 6.04s
/work 200 6.04s
/healthz 200 5.40s
```

The replica logs `GET /healthz 200 2.7ms` for the last call. The rest of the 5.40s is spent waiting for a free slot.

The built-in routes do not cover this case. The proxy's `/-/healthz` reports whether the proxy is draining, has a route table and, on worker nodes, knows a running replica. The replica's `/-/healthz` exists only with direct ingress, which `RAY_SERVE_ENABLE_DIRECT_INGRESS` leaves off by default. It returns the result of the controller's last `check_health` call. Neither runs a request through the application. #33979 asked for a per-application route that calls `check_health`. It was closed in a backlog sweep for inactivity.

Two possible shapes:

- An option on `@serve.ingress` or `@serve.deployment` that lists routes exempt from `max_ongoing_requests`, e.g. `exempt_routes=["/healthz"]`.
- A per-application `/{route_prefix}/-/healthz` that calls `check_health` outside the request semaphore.

Documented guidance on the recommended pattern would also work.

### Use case

A FastAPI ingress deployment forwards each request to model deployments through handles. Each forwarded call takes several seconds. A container health check calls the app's `/healthz`, which reports `serve.status()`. With the default `max_ongoing_requests=5`, five concurrent calls left `/healthz` unroutable. The health check failed. The container supervisor then restarted the service, which failed every in-flight request. Raising `max_ongoing_requests` to 200 only moves the threshold. A separate health deployment does not exercise the ingress deployment that serves the traffic.

items.title: [Core] GCS main thread wastes time copying redundant cluster resource data
items.author: dancingactor
items.body_excerpt:
## Description
On every RaySyncer update and every GCS load pull, the GCS main thread redundantly copies each node's resource data into `GcsResourceManager::node_resource_usages_`, even though the same data is already stored in `ClusterResourceManager` and `GcsAutoscalerStateManager`. On large clusters, these copies take a significant share of the GCS main thread.

## Performance Impact

I ran some performance tests.

Test configuration:
- Resources per node: 6
- Demand shapes per node: 10
- Busy cluster: both RaySyncer and GCS load pulls run at their maximum update rates
  - RaySyncer: 10 updates/node/s
  - GCS load pull: 1 pull/node/s

#### 1. In a large cluster (5,000 nodes), these redundant copies take an extra 26% overhead of the GCS main thread.

| Nodes | Main thread cost (with redundant copy) | Main thread cost (without copy) | Extra cost |
| ----- | -------------------------------------- | ------------------------------- | ---------- |
| 100   | 1.1%                                   | 0.8%                            | +0.3%      |
| 1,000 | 12.6%                                  | 9.1%                            | +3.6%      |
| 5,000 | 79.5%                                  | 53.7%                           | +25.8%     |

#### 2. Looking only at the resource data update work in GCS, the redundant copy makes it 34–48% more expensive.

| Nodes | Update cost (with redundant copy) | Update cost (without copy) | Extra cost |
| ----- | ----------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- | ------------------------------ |
| 100   | 11.1 ms/s                                       | 8.3 ms/s                                 | +34%                           |
| 1,000 | 126.5 ms/s                                      | 90.8 ms/s                                | +39%                           |
| 5,000 | 795.0 ms/s                                      | 536.9 ms/s                               | +48%                           |

## Proposed Changes
Remove the extra copy of resource data in GCS, `GcsResourceManager::node_resource_usages_`. 

Proposed steps:

1. Migrate the consumers of `GcsResourceManager::node_resource_usages_` to other data sources.
   - **Autoscaler v1(#66633)**: it currently reads resource demand and placement group load from `GcsResourceManager::node_resource_usages_`.
     - **Resource demand:** `GcsAutoscalerStateManager` already exposes an equivalent field (`pending_resource_requests` in `ClusterResourceState`), so the v1 autoscaler can use it directly.
     - **Placement group load:** `GcsAutoscalerStateManager` only exposes the derived `pending_gang_resource_requests`, not the raw `PlacementGroupTableData` that the v1 autoscaler needs. Add a `placement_group_load` field to `ClusterResourceState` in `autoscaler.proto` so `GcsAutoscalerStateManager` can expose it directly.

2. Remove `GcsResourceManager::node_resource_usages_` and its related methods.

items.title: Autoscaler-driven elastic expert/data parallelism for MoE
items.author: Jeffwan
items.body_excerpt:
### Feature Description and Motivation

For large MoE models we only scale whole replicas, which is coarse and expensive. vLLM has elastic EP (`enable_elastic_ep`, `/is_scaling_elastic_ep`, the DP coordinator request-wave protocol in `vllm/v1/engine/coordinator.py`) to add/remove DP/EP ranks at runtime. The autoscaler doesn't drive it. Scaling EP width by load would right-size MoE serving without full-replica steps.

### Use Case

DeepSeek / Qwen-MoE style deployments where per-replica cost is high and traffic varies; scale expert parallelism up and down instead of adding or removing entire replicas.

### Proposed Solution

Let PodAutoscaler target EP/DP width for elastic-EP-enabled deployments and drive scaling via the engine's elastic-EP endpoints + the DP coordinator wave protocol. Start observe-only (read `/is_scaling_elastic_ep` and wave state) before acting on it.

items.title: feat: Add AIBrix Chat - a frontend demo portal for LLM inference
items.author: Jeffwan
items.body_excerpt:
### 🚀 Feature Description and Motivation

AIBrix provides powerful infrastructure for LLM inference, but we lack a user-facing demo to showcase its capabilities. Currently, users need to interact with AIBrix through API calls, or third-party clients, which creates friction when:

- Live demos — Presenting AIBrix at conferences, meetups, or internal reviews requires a polished UI
- End-to-end validation — Testing the full stack (gateway routing, model serving, load balancing) benefits from a real frontend client
- Onboarding — A working chat UI makes it easier for new contributors to understand the user-facing value of the infrastructure

### Use Case

Add a lightweight chat portal under apps/chat/web/ that serves as both a demo and a functional frontend for AIBrix-managed LLM endpoints.

What it includes:
- Chat interface with conversation management (create, search, delete, move)
- Project organization for grouping related conversations
- Model selector supporting multiple backends
- Sidebar navigation with chat history
- Dark-themed, responsive UI built with React + Vite + Tailwind CSS


Architecture:
```
  apps/
  ├── chat/
   │   ├── web/          # React frontend
   │   └── api/          # Backend proxy for LLM endpoints (planned)
```

### Proposed Solution

Why in-repo (not a separate project)?

1. Dogfooding — The chat portal consumes AIBrix gateway APIs directly, validating routing algorithms, model selection, and streaming behavior from a real client
2. Faster iteration — Co-locating with infrastructure code means API and frontend changes can land together
3. Visibility — Contributors are more likely to maintain something that lives alongside the core project
4. Demo-ready — A single repo clone gives users everything needed for a complete demo

### Task break down

items.title: JIT `topk` module ignores `FLASHINFER_CUDA_ARCH_LIST`: hardcoded `sm89_nvcc_flags` produce an sm_89-only binary
items.author: jhcdlg
items.body_excerpt:
> Filing against flashinfer (this is where the root cause is). We hit it through SGLang,
> which is why the reproduction below mentions SGLang  -  but the mechanism is entirely in
> `flashinfer/jit/`.

## Environment

- `flashinfer` **0.6.18** (installed via SGLang `main`, HEAD `5e9342d`, 2026-09-18)
- Two GPUs in one host, TP=2: **RTX 3080 (sm_86)** + RTX 4080 SUPER (sm_89)
- CUDA 13.0, torch 2.13.0+cu130, Python 3.11.16
- flashinfer JIT nvcc: **13.4 (V13.4.59, from the pip `nvidia/cu13` package)**  -  i.e. *not*
  the 13.0 that `torch.version.cuda` reports. The build metadata baked into the artifacts
  scanned below reads `Cuda compilation tools, 13.4, V13.4.59`.
- `FLASHINFER_CUDA_ARCH_LIST="8.6 8.9"` was **set** in the environment
- `FLASHINFER_EXTRA_CUDAFLAGS` was also tried, with `-gencode` for both 86 and 89  -  **no effect** on this issue

## Summary

The JIT-compiled `topk` module ships the hardcoded flag list `sm89_nvcc_flags`
(`flashinfer/jit/core.py`  -  line 123 in 0.6.18, which is the version we hit this on; the same
list is at line 156 on current `main`), which contains an explicit
`-gencode=arch=compute_89,code=sm_89`. `flashinfer/jit/cpp_ext.py:216` (same line in 0.6.18 and
on `main`) then decides that
**a module which already carries its own `-gencode` should not get the architecture list
appended**  -  so `FLASHINFER_CUDA_ARCH_LIST` is silently ignored for that module only.

Result: `topk.so` is built for sm_89 alone. On any other architecture it fails at **run
time**, not build time  -  and the failure surfaces on the *first real inference request*,
while the server looks perfectly healthy.

## Symptom (this part is what makes it expensive to diagnose)

- The server **starts normally**: `Uvicorn running`, `/v1/models` returns 200, weights
  loaded, no warning anywhere in the log.
- **Every real inference request fails.** `num_running_reqs` and `kv_used_tokens` stay **0**
  the whole time  -  the request never reaches the scheduler, so the first thing anyone
  suspects is the frontend / networking, not a kernel.
- The log accumulates (18 occurrences in our run):

```
RuntimeError: Check failed: (status == cudaSuccess) is false:
TopK failed with error code no kernel image is available for execution on the device
```

- A handful of other ops (`BatchPrefillWithPagedKVCache`) fail the same way, which is what
  made us first chase the *general* `FLASHINFER_CUDA_ARCH_LIST` question instead of
  looking at a per-module override.

## Where the message comes from

```
flashinfer/data/csrc/topk.cu:84:
    TVM_FFI_ICHECK(status == cudaSuccess)
      << "TopK failed with error code " << cudaGetErrorString(status);
```

Not torch: `torch.topk` works fine on sm_86 here  -  we tested 6 variants (different dtypes
and k values) on that GPU, all OK. So it is specifically flashinfer's JIT `topk` module.

## Decisive evidence: scan the architectures actually compiled into each JIT artifact

Scanning every `.so` under `~/.cache/sglang/.cache/flashinfer/0.6.18/86_89/cached_ops/`:

| Artifact | Architectures present | sm_86 usable? |
|---|---|---|
| `sampling/sampling.so` | **86, 89** | yes |
| `batch_prefill_with_kv_cache.../*.so` | **86, 89** | yes |
| **`topk/topk.so`** | **89 only** | no |

Everything else in the same cache directory got both architectures. Only `topk` did not.

## Root cause

```python
# flashinfer/jit/core.py:123   -  a hardcoded per-architecture flag list
sm89_nvcc_flags = ["-gencode=arch=compute_89,code=sm_89", "-DFLASHINFER_ENABLE_FP8_E8M0"]
```

```python
# flashinfer/jit/cpp_ext.py:216   -  if the module brings its own -gencode, the arch list is not appended
module_has_gencode = any(flag.startswith("-gencode=") for flag in extra_cuda_cflags)
```

`topk` is one of the modules that carries `sm89_nvcc_flags`, so it hits both: the module
declares sm_89 explicitly, and the general mechanism declines to add anything else.
`FLASHINFER_CUDA_ARCH_LIST="8.6 8.9"` therefore has no effect on this module.

Because the user-facing env var is documented as *the* way to control target
architectures, this failure mode is very hard to reason about from the outside: the same env
var works for `sampling` and `batch_prefill` in the very same build.

## Suggested fix direction

- Generate these per-architecture flag lists **from** the effective arch list instead of
  hardcoding a single `-gencode`, or
- In `cpp_ext.py`, treat a module's own `-gencode` as **additive** (append the arch list
  rather than skipping it), or at minimum warn when the two disagree  -  right now the
  mismatch is completely silent.
- A warning when the compiled artifact's architecture set does not cover the GPUs actually
  present would have saved us a lot of time.

## Impact / who else hits this

Anyone running flashinfer **0.6.18** on a GPU that is not sm_89  -  e.g. sm_86 (RTX 30-series),
sm_80 (A100), sm_75  -  **for the `topk` op path**. We only verified sm_86, and only on one
host, so we do not want to overstate the breadth; but the mechanism is architecture-list
logic, not hardware-specific.

Note that on our machine **a single-GPU run using only the 4080 SUPER (sm_89) works fine**  - 
the failure needs a non-sm_89 device to be part of the run. So a mixed-architecture host
fails on every request, while the same software on a single sm_89 card is completely healthy.

## Caveats

- Verified on one host, two architectures (sm_86 + sm_89), one flashinfer version (0.6.18).
- We did not bisect which flashinfer release introduced `sm89_nvcc_flags` for `topk`.
- Our evidence for "the arch list is ignored" is the built artifact's architecture set plus
  the source lines above  -  we did not instrument the JIT build to print the final nvcc
  command line. If that would help, we are happy to re-run with more logging.

## Workaround we are using

Remove the non-sm_89 GPU from the run (i.e. use a single sm_89 card), which sidesteps the
`topk` module entirely. Not viable for us long-term since our workload needs TP a

items.title: [Bug] Autotuner: rank-dependent MoE cache keys deadlock warm starts under set_autotune_process_group
items.author: qiching
items.body_excerpt:
### Before submitting

- [x] I have searched existing issues and did not find a solution or an existing report.

### Environment

- FlashInfer 0.6.18.post1 and 0.7.0.post1, with vLLM (vllm-project/vllm#57423).
- Reported on 8×H100 (TP8/EP8), 2× RTX PRO 5000 (TP2) and two-node DGX Spark (TP2).

### Bug description

Under `set_autotune_process_group`, a cache hit skips that profile's timing all-reduce, so every rank in the group must hit or miss the same profiles. The CUTLASS `MoERunner` (`flashinfer/fused_moe/core.py`) puts `tp_rank`, `ep_rank` and `cluster_rank` in `get_cache_key_extras`, so the same cache file hits on some ranks but not others, and the ranks that miss block in the reduce. vLLM broadcasts rank 0's cache file to every rank, so warm restarts hang (vllm-project/vllm#57423). #6006 removes these fields.

`CuteDslFusedMoERunner` (`flashinfer/fused_moe/cute_dsl/tuner.py`) keys on `local_expert_offset`, which vLLM's `flashinfer_cutedsl` MoE backend sets to `ep_rank * local_num_experts`, so its cache keys also differ across EP ranks. Not reproduced yet.

### Minimal reproduction

1. Start vLLM with a FlashInfer CUTLASS MoE model at TP≥2 with a persistent cache directory; the autotune cache is saved.
2. Restart with the same configuration: rank 0 gets config-file cache hits, the other ranks start tuning, and startup hangs.

### Error messages / logs

~~~text
(Worker_TP0) [Autotuner]: Config cache hit for trtllm::fused_moe::gemm1 (runner=MoERunner, source=config file)
(Worker_TP1) [AutoTuner]: Tuning trtllm::fused_moe::gemm1:   0%|          | 0/22 [00:00<?, ?profile/s]
...
(Worker_TP1) [AutoTuner]: Tuning trtllm::fused_moe::gemm1:   0%|          | 0/22 [30:01<?, ?profile/s]
~~~

### Additional context

Fix: drop rank-dependent values from the persisted cache key, as #6006 does for CUTLASS, and do the same for `CuteDslFusedMoERunner` (`CuteDslFusedMoEW4A16Runner` keys on `local_expert_offset` too). CuTe-DSL MoE owners: please confirm the offset doesn't affect tactic validity.

Related: vllm-project/vllm#57423, vllm-project/vllm#57635, #6006

items.title: [Bug]: Qwen3.8-27B NVFP4 cannot load with the PyTorch backend
items.author: mihai-chiorean
items.body_excerpt:
### System Info

- TensorRT-LLM: current `main`
- Backend: PyTorch
- Model: `unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4`
- Reproduced on: DGX Spark / SM121

### Who can help?

_No response_

### Information

- [x] The official example scripts
- [x] The `transformers` checkpoint loader
- [x] The PyTorch backend

### Reproduction

Attempt to load the checkpoint through `LLM(...)` or `trtllm-serve` with the PyTorch backend and text-only multimodal execution (`disable_mm_encoder=True`).

The checkpoint is a dense Qwen3.8/Qwen3.5-family VLM with mixed compressed-tensors quantization: packed NVFP4 dense MLP weights, FP8 attention/GDN/lm_head weights, FP8 KV cache, and one MTP layer.

### Expected behavior

The checkpoint should select `Qwen3_5VLModel`, preserve each config group's quantization, map packed compressed-tensors names to TRT-LLM parameters, construct a rowwise-FP8 `lm_head`, and generate coherent text with and without MTP.

### Actual behavior

Current `main` has several independent blockers:

1. Generic dense Qwen3.6/3.8 VLM configs are classified as Qwen-Image-Bench configs.
2. The compressed-tensors parser rejects or loses multiple `config_groups`.
3. Packed NVFP4 names/scales are not normalized for the Qwen mapper.
4. Dense MLP quant-config keys do not match the `_DenseMlpAdapter` runtime module path.
5. The explicit FP8 `lm_head` entry is dropped, which would cast the FP8 weight to bf16 and discard its scale.

### Validation

With focused fixes for those concerns, an SM121 full-model smoke loaded 23.91 GiB of model weights, selected native `trtllm::nvfp4_gemm`, constructed `lm_head` as `FP8_PER_CHANNEL_PER_TOKEN`, and generated coherent 64-token responses for two prompts. The same stack also generated coherently with the checkpoint MTP layer enabled.

The changes will be proposed as small dependent PRs so each concern can be reviewed independently.

items.title: EngineDeadError message compounds a prefix each time it is unpickled
items.author: StephenLReed
items.body_excerpt:
### System Info

- TensorRT-LLM: 1.3.0rc23 (built from `f20ea652`); behaviour re-checked against `main` @ `fbda11f5`
- GPU: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090 (sm_120), driver 595.71.05
- PyTorch 2.11.0+cu130, CUDA 13.0, Python 3.12.13
- Ubuntu 25.10, kernel 6.17.0-41-generic
- Backend: PyTorch; single GPU, no TP/PP
- Model where observed: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4 with FP8 KV cache (where model-specific)

### Who can help?

_No response_

### Reproduction

`EngineDeadError.__init__` renders `root_cause` into the message, and default exception pickling
round-trips through `args` — which holds that rendered message. Unpickling re-invokes `__init__` with
the message string as the cause, so the prefix is prepended again on every hop:

```
original : Engine has died: RuntimeError: PyExecutor has already been shutdown
1 hop    : Engine has died: str: Engine has died: RuntimeError: PyExecutor has already been shutdown
2 hops   : Engine has died: str: Engine has died: str: Engine has died: RuntimeError: ...
```

The class is raised when a worker process dies, i.e. exactly where it crosses a process boundary, so
the mangled text is the form users are most likely to encounter.

### Expected behavior

An EngineDeadError reconstructed in another process renders the same message as the original.

### actual behavior

Each unpickle prepends the prefix again, so the message grows one 'Engine has died: str: ' per hop. .root_cause is unaffected.

### additional notes

Message only. `__dict__` is restored after `__init__`, so `.root_cause` survives as the original
exception and the attribute contract holds. This is log legibility and unbounded message growth, not
a broken consumer contract.

Add `__reduce__` returning `(self.__class__, (self.root_cause,))` so reconstruction uses the cause
rather than the rendered text. `root_cause` is already pickled as part of `__dict__`, so no new
picklability requirement is introduced.

We have the patch with four CPU-only tests (2 fail before, 4 pass after) and are raising this Issue
Request first per CONTRIBUTING.md.

**Questions for maintainers**

1. Would you prefer `__reduce__`, or moving the rendering out of `__init__` into `__str__` so `args`
   never holds the formatted text?
2. Are there other exception types in `tensorrt_llm/executor` that render constructor arguments into
   the message and would have the same issue?

items.title: [RFC] Training/Inference Numerical Consistency for RL Post-Training
items.author: shikicloud
items.body_excerpt:
## Motivation

In RL post-training, the rollout engine samples tokens and the trainer recomputes logprobs on those same tokens with the same weights. When the two disagree, PPO's importance ratio is computed against the wrong denominator; low-probability tokens can spike the ratio and blow up gradients; training can collapse.

Four causes, each with published evidence:

1. **Kernels are not batch-invariant.** The same request can produce different logits depending on what else is in the batch, because RMSNorm/matmul/attention pick their reduction strategy from batch shape ([Thinking Machines, "Defeating Nondeterminism in LLM Inference"](https://thinkingmachines.ai/blog/defeating-nondeterminism-in-llm-inference/), 2025-09-10).
2. **MoE routing disagrees between engines even with identical weights** — ~10% of per-layer routing decisions differ, 94% of tokens affected in ≥1 layer, on Qwen3-30B-A3B ([R3 paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.11370), arXiv 2510.11370). R3 (#18397) is an initial solution to fix this cause.
3. **LM-head / router precision.** BF16 alone dropped train/inference token-probability correlation to ~0.9; FP32 restored ~0.99 ([MiniMax-M1 tech report](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.13585), arXiv 2506.13585).
4. **Severity is hardware- and kernel-dependent and compounds with length.** Same code: KL ≈ 5e-4–1e-3 on one GPU, 1e-2–1e-1 on another, traced to a specific attention-kernel bug ([ByteDance Seed, "When Speed Kills Stability"](https://yingru.notion.site/When-Speed-Kills-Stability-Demystifying-RL-Collapse-from-the-Training-Inference-Mismatch-271211a558b7808d8b12d403fd15edda)).

R3 addresses cause 2. This RFC covers what's left of R3 (cause 2's remaining edges) plus causes 1, 3, and a sampling-semantics issue that compounds all of them. Other useful features like TIS/MIS/KPop remain in RL frameworks but not inference engines. Futhermore, this RFC targets on important features for TRTLLM, we will explore new features to solve this problem on an new issue.

This RFC is generated by codex with human's instructions and supervision. Also thanks @NolenLiang and @JeffPengCoder's help. CC's @joyang-nv @xuantengh @yuki-97 

## What exists today

- **Router Replay**: `LlmArgs.enable_return_routed_experts` + `SamplingParams.return_routed_experts` → `CompletionOutput.routed_experts`, `int16`, `[seq_len-1, num_moe_layers, top_k]`, pre-EPLB logical ids. Separated-routing MoE backends only; fails closed on PP>1, spec decode, fused routing(TBD).
- **`logprobs_mode`**: `RAW` (pre-sampling-params) / `PROCESSED` (post). No `raw_logits`/`processed_logits` variants.
- **`FORCE_DETERMINISTIC`**: a C++ env var, not exposed via `LlmArgs`. Covers attention multi-block, KV-cache reuse, and all-reduce workspace size. Does not cover autotuner tactic selection, FMHA library selection, all-reduce *strategy* selection, or CUDA-graph padding(TBD).
- **`MoeConfig.disable_finalize_fusion`**: CUTLASS only; the LlmArgs docstring states the fused path is non-deterministic for top-k > 2.

Two items already landed for Router Replay: per-request gating (`SamplingParams.return_routed_experts=False` now correctly attaches nothing), and the output dtype is `int16`.

Reading the PyTorch backend (`tensorrt_llm/_torch/`) turns up nine places where a numeric result depends on batch shape or token count, not just the sequence — this is what drives the Deterministic inference work below:

| # | Source | Class | Covered by `FORCE_DETERMINISTIC`? |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Attention multi-block/split-KV (MMHA/XQA/TRTLLM-Gen); split count = `f(SM_count, batch*heads)` | batch-dependent | Yes — but a shared-memory guard can silently re-enable multi-block regardless of the flag |
| 2 | FMHA library selection by batch bucket (`fmha/manager.py`) | batch-dependent | No — `TLLM_FMHA_LIBS` can pin one manually |
| 3 | Dense GEMM tactic selection by M (autotuner) | batch-dependent, plus profiling-noise without a persisted cache | No — `enable_autotuner=False` falls back to `tactic=-1`, but the fallback cuBLASLt path's own algorithm choice is unexamined |
| 4 | MoE grouped-GEMM tactic selection by token count | batch-dependent | No |
| 5 | MoE finalize/unpermute reduction, CUTLASS top-k>2 | non-deterministic per LlmArgs docstring | Partially — `disable_finalize_fusion=True`; TRTLLM-Gen has no unfused path |
| 6 | All-reduce *strategy* selection by message size | batch-dependent | No — only workspace *size* is fixed, strategy selection isn't |
| 7 | CUDA-graph batch-size padding ladder | batch-dependent | No |
| 8 | Chunked-prefill / KV-reuse boundary placement | depends on scheduler budget, not just the sequence | Yes — both disabled |

Two bugs found while reading the same code, independent of scope: `getBoolEnv` matches only the exact string `"1"` (`FORCE_DETERMINISTIC=true` is silently ignored), and MMHA's multi-block override under shared-memory pressure bypasses the flag entirely.

## Proposed Change.

Organized by delivery phase. Each phase lists what happens to every workstream in that phase, rather than each workstream carrying its own separate phase numbering.

### Phase 1 — config only, no new kernels, land first

- **Router Replay:**
  - Validate TRTLLM-Gen, DeepGEMM, and WideEP end to end. Today only CUTLASS has a GPU test, on Qwen1.5-MoE-A2.7B-Chat; the other backends' support is inferred from `_supports_load_balancer()`, not tested.
  - Optional `uint8` output for `num_experts <= 256` models. `int16` already halves the naive `int32` footprint, but large payloads are a real failure mode at scale — a comparable rollout system hit ~35GB/actor, ~280GB across 8 actors, on a 96-layer MoE model with long context. Worth having the compact path ready before someone hits this on TRT-LLM.
- **Deterministic inference:**
  - Config-only surface over the gaps in the table above:

    ```python
    class TorchLlmArgs:
        enable_deterministic_inference: bool = False
        # Superset of FORCE_DETERMINISTIC=1:
        #   - autotuner f

items.title: [Bug] sm12x MoE CuTe-DSL kernels are never disk-cached — cute.compile hardcodes no_cache=True, so every fresh engine re-pays 15–40 s MLIR compiles per kernel shape
items.author: jhsmith409
items.body_excerpt:
## Summary

The Blackwell sm12x fused-MoE path compiles all of its CuTe-DSL kernels through explicit
`cute.compile(...)`, which unconditionally disables the DSL's file cache. The only caching
layer is three in-process Python dicts, so **every engine start re-pays the full MLIR JIT
cost for every kernel specialization it touches** — measured at **~40 s** for the dynamic
kernel's first hit and **~15–18 s per small-`m` micro-kernel specialization**. In a serving
context (vLLM `--moe-backend=flashinfer_b12x`) these compiles land mid-request and freeze
the whole engine (vllm#47458: ~17.5 s stop-the-world stalls, all in-flight requests frozen
including mid-decode).

`CUTE_DSL_CACHE_DIR` / `CUTE_DSL_DISABLE_FILE_CACHING` have no effect on this path — the
gate that would consult them is short-circuited before they are read.

## Environment

- flashinfer 0.6.12, 0.6.13, and **0.6.15.post1** (all verified; `moe_dispatch.py` cache
  structure unchanged across them)
- nvidia-cutlass-dsl 4.5.0 and **4.6.0** (both verified)
- SM120: RTX 5070 Ti (×2, TP/PP), RTX 5090 (unsharded), RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell — reproduced
  on all three in the vllm#47458 thread
- Model: `nvidia/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4` via vLLM `--moe-backend=flashinfer_b12x`

## Mechanism (exact code paths)

1. **The DSL hardcodes `no_cache=True` for explicit compiles.**
   `CompileCallable._compile` sets `kwargs["no_cache"] = True` unconditionally:
   - nvidia-cutlass-dsl 4.5.0: `base_dsl/compiler.py:604-605`
   - nvidia-cutlass-dsl 4.6.0: `base_dsl/compiler.py:1319`

2. **The file cache is gated behind `if not no_cache`** — both the load and the dump —
   so the env vars are never even consulted for explicit compiles:
   - 4.5.0: `base_dsl/dsl.py:1645` (load), `:1736` (dump)
   - 4.6.0: `base_dsl/dsl.py:2004` (load), `:2105` (dump); in-memory `jit_cache` lookups
     likewise skipped under `no_cache` at `:2012`, `:2293`

3. **The sm12x MoE dispatch only ever compiles through `cute.compile`,** with plain
   in-process dicts on top — nothing reaches disk:
   - 0.6.12/0.6.13: `blackwell_sm12x/moe_dispatch.py:676/912/1675` (compile sites);
     `_STATIC/_MICRO/_DYNAMIC_KERNEL_CACHE`
   - 0.6.15.post1: compile sites at `:697/:942/:1723`; caches at `:486/:733/:1524`

4. Compounding factor (tracked separately as #3836): the micro-kernel `cache_key`
   includes both `m` and `workspace.max_rows` (0.6.15.post1 `moe_dispatch.py:770-791`,
   fields at `:774`/`:778`), so workspace growth invalidates already-compiled small-batch
   entries even *within* a process lifetime. With no disk layer underneath, each
   invalidation is a full 15 s+ recompile, not a reload.

## Verification

Behavioral check from the vllm#47458 thread (credit @waynehacking8, on 0.6.12 / DSL 4.5.0):

- `cute.compile` of a trivial `@cute.jit` function leaves `CUTE_DSL_CACHE_DIR` **empty**.
- Calling the same jit function **directly** (implicit compile path) writes
  `cute_dsl_<hash>.mlir`, and a fresh process then logs `JIT cache hit IN-FILE`.
- Only the implicit direct-call path caches; flashinfer's MoE dispatch never uses it.

Source-level re-verification on 0.6.15.post1 / DSL 4.6.0 (2026-08-02, inside the
`vllm/vllm-openai` nightly image): every line cite in the Mechanism section above was
confirmed against the installed packages — the hardcoded `no_cache=True`, the
`if not no_cache` gates around both file-cache load and dump, the three `cute.compile`
sites, the three in-process dicts, and `m`/`max_rows` still present in the micro-kernel
cache key.

Measured first-hit compile costs (RTX PRO 6000, synthetic MoE E=32/topk=4 driving
`B12xMoEWrapper.run` exactly as vLLM's `FlashInferB12xExperts` does):

| kernel path | first hit | subsequent (same key) |
|---|---|---|
| dynamic (m-independent key) | ~40 s | 1–3 ms |
| micro m=1 | 14.9 s | ms |
| micro m=2 | 15.2 s | ms |
| micro m=64 | 18.3 s | ms |

Production symptom: vllm#47458 — py-spy captured 16 consecutive samples over 8.35 s pinned
in `b12x_fused_moe (flashinfer/fused_moe/cute_dsl/b12x_moe.py:166)` during a live
~17.5 s engine-wide stall; `perf` showed `_cutlass_ir.cpython-312.so` frames present only
during stalls.

## Why this deserves a disk layer even after #3836

#3836 stops *rekeying* (recompiles within one process). But serving engines restart —
deploys, config changes, crash recovery, autoscaling — and each fresh process re-pays the
entire compile set: ~40 s dynamic + 15–18 s per small-shape class. For a model like
Qwen3.6-35B-A3B this is 1–2 minutes of mid-serving stalls per engine lifetime that a
disk cache would reduce to milliseconds. The artifacts are deterministic products of
(kernel source, shape/config tuple, DSL version, arch) — exactly what file caches are for.

## Suggested fix directions

Either would resolve it; the first is contained entirely in flashinfer:

1. **flashinfer grows its own disk layer for sm12x MoE kernels**: serialize the compiled
   artifact keyed by the existing `cache_key` tuples + flashinfer version +
   nvidia-cutlass-dsl version + SM arch, under `FLASHINFER_WORKSPACE_DIR` (or a new env),
   loading into `_STATIC/_MICRO/_DYNAMIC_KERNEL_CACHE` on miss. The DSL's own
   `compile_and_cache` machinery demonstrates the artifact is serializable (the implicit
   path already writes/reads `.mlir` + compiled objects).
2. **Upstream: nvidia-cutlass-dsl honors its file cache under explicit `cute.compile`**
   (stop hardcoding `no_cache=True`, or add an opt-in kwarg flashinfer can pass).

A third, cheaper-but-partial option is an official warm-up API (the attempt in
vllm#47599 was closed unmerged): it moves the cost to boot but still re-pays it every
process start, and needs the largest-workspace-first ordering to avoid #3836 rekeying —
a disk cache composes with, rather than replaces, that.

## Cross-references

- vllm#47458 — serving-stall report this splits from (mechanism established in-thread by
  @waynehacking8; py-spy confirmation by me)
- flashinfer#3836 — the workspace-rekeying half (open)

items.title: [Bug] CuTe-DSL MXFP8 quantization zeros nonzero BF16 blocks when E8M0 scale byte is 0
items.author: youngeunkwon0405
items.body_excerpt:
### Before submitting

- [x] I searched existing issues and pull requests and did not find an open report or fix for this exact CuTe-DSL scale-byte-0 case. Related reports are listed below.

### Bug description

`flashinfer.mxfp8_quantize(..., backend="cute-dsl")` turns nonzero, exactly representable BF16 values into zero when it selects E8M0 scale byte `0`.

E8M0 byte `0` represents **2^-127**, not zero. Quantization should therefore use the finite FP32 inverse scale **2^127**. The CuTe-DSL inverse-scale helper instead explicitly returns zero for this code, so the FP8 payloads become zero.

This reproduces on FlashInfer **0.6.18**, NVIDIA **GB200**, CUDA **13.4**, PyTorch **2.14.0a0+b2c75dd062.nv26.09**, and **nvidia-cutlass-dsl 4.6.2** as reported by `importlib.metadata.version()` in the reproducer. The same zero override is present in the inspected main revision `46340689a5ab5665ab39f6281dac4d021d7ae94b`; I have not run that main revision.

The synthetic inputs below are all **normal BF16 values**, so this loss does not come from BF16 underflow. They are also exactly representable in MXFP8 E4M3. No model weights, TE dequantization, or external scale-byte postprocessing is involved in this reproduction.

### Minimal reproduction

```python
import torch
import flashinfer

# Four constant 32-value blocks per row; the last is a control.
s = 2.0 ** -127
values = torch.tensor([20*s, -20*s, 448*s, 448*2*s], dtype=torch.float64)
x = values.to(device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16).repeat_interleave(32).repeat(32, 1)
assert torch.equal(x[0, ::32].double().cpu(), values)

q, sf = flashinfer.mxfp8_quantize(
    x, backend="cute-dsl", is_sf_swizzled_layout=False, alignment=32
)
sf = sf.reshape(32, 4)
# Independent FP64 decode: E8M0 byte 0 is a valid nonzero scale.
scale = torch.exp2(sf.double() - 127).repeat_interleave(32, dim=1)
decoded = q.double() * scale

print("input:", x[0, ::32].double().tolist())
print("scale bytes:", sf[0].tolist())
print("FP8 payload:", q[0, ::32].float().tolist())
print("decoded:", decoded[0, ::32].tolist())
print("changed elements:", (decoded != x.double()).sum().item(), "/", x.numel())
print("control exact:", torch.equal(decoded[:, 96:], x[:, 96:].double()))
```

### Actual and expected results

The verified run produced:

```text
input: [1.1754943508222875e-37, -1.1754943508222875e-37, 2.633107345841924e-36, 5.266214691683848e-36]
scale bytes: [0, 0, 0, 1]
FP8 payload: [0.0, -0.0, 0.0, 448.0]
decoded: [0.0, -0.0, 0.0, 5.266214691683848e-36]
changed elements: 3072 / 4096
control exact: True
```

For the selected scale bytes `[0, 0, 0, 1]`, the expected payloads are `[20.0, -20.0, 448.0, 448.0]`, giving **zero changed elements**. The scale-byte-1 control already passes.

### Suspected cause and requested fix

The [inverse-scale helper](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/blob/46340689a5ab5665ab39f6281dac4d021d7ae94b/flashinfer/quantization/quantization_cute_dsl_utils.py#L209-L242) constructs the exponent for `2^(127 - code)`, then overrides the result with `0` when `code == 0`. For code 0, the initially constructed value `2^127` is finite and is the required multiplier.

Could you fix the code-0 inverse-scale handling and add regression coverage that checks preservation of nonzero values, including positive/negative constant blocks and an all-zero block? Checking only for the absence of NaNs does not catch this loss. The helper is shared with MXFP4, so its callers would also benefit from boundary coverage; this report's GPU reproduction covers MXFP8 E4M3 only.

### Related TE fix and FlashInfer reports

- **[NVIDIA/TransformerEngine#3262](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TransformerEngine/pull/3262)**, merged August 5, fixes the related E8M0 code-0 decoding bug: the forward scale expansion must produce `2^-127` rather than zero. This is the same format-boundary problem in a different operation: TE fixes forward scale expansion during dequantization; FlashInfer needs the inverse scale `2^127` during quantization.
- **#4023** fixes inverse-scale handling for **code 254** and explicitly retains the code-0 zero override, so it does not address this reproduction.
- **#2440 / #2441** address tiny-input NaNs in the CUDA path by producing zeros. The issue here is preserving valid nonzero values in the CuTe-DSL path.

### Environment

Collected with `python -m flashinfer.collect_env` in the same venv/container used for the reproduction. Private checkout, venv, and cache paths are replaced with placeholders; package and library information is retained.

The venv inherits system-site packages. The reproducer directly reported `importlib.metadata.version("nvidia-cutlass-dsl") == "4.6.2"` and `importlib.metadata.version("apache-tvm-ffi") == "0.1.11"`. The collector's package inventory below enumerates all visible distributions into a dictionary, so the inherited system versions `4.8.0.dev0` and `0.1.14` overwrite those entries in its display. Both observations are included here to make the environment explicit.

<details>
<summary>Full environment report (private paths redacted)</summary>

```text
### FlashInfer environment report
<!-- generated by `python -m flashinfer.collect_env`; paste into your issue -->

==== FlashInfer ====
flashinfer                   : 0.6.18
flashinfer commit            : 69ff11fc4954396d98326656dc85debd2223f637
flashinfer file              : <venv>/lib/python3.12/site-packages/flashinfer/__init__.py
flashinfer-cubin             : not installed
flashinfer-jit-cache         : not installed
JIT cache                    : <jit-cache-base>/.cache/flashinfer (0 compiled .so)
Cubin store (local)          : <jit-cache-base>/.cache/flashinfer/cubins (0 cubins, 0 MiB)
Target CUDA archs (resolved) : {(10, '0a')}

items.title: [Bug]: MiniMax-M2 streaming tool parser re-sends full arguments and duplicates the tool call
items.author: MohammadHijjawi97
items.body_excerpt:
### System Info

CPU only (parser logic, no GPU needed); TensorRT-LLM main @ 534e1f8a.

### Who can help?

_No response_

### Information

- [ ] The official example scripts
- [x] My own modified scripts

### Reproduction

With `--tool_parser minimax_m2` and `stream=true`, a tool call that streams over several chunks produces broken output. Minimal repro without a model: feed this text to `MiniMaxM2ToolParser.parse_streaming_increment` in 4-character chunks:

```
<minimax:tool_call><invoke name="get_weather"><parameter name="city">Paris</parameter><parameter name="unit">celsius</parameter></invoke></minimax:tool_call>
```

### Expected behavior

The concatenated `function.arguments` deltas form `{"city": "Paris", "unit": "celsius"}`, and there is a single tool call (index 0) — the same result as the non-streaming `detect_and_parse`.

### actual behavior

- The full arguments JSON is re-sent each time a parameter completes, so the concatenated deltas are `{"city": "Paris"}{"city": "Paris", "unit": "celsius"}` (invalid JSON).
- When `</invoke>` arrives, the function name is emitted again under tool index 1, creating a phantom second call.

### additional notes

The partial-invoke regex can also match across an already-closed `<invoke>` and emit a garbage tool name. I have a fix with a regression test and will open a PR.

items.title: [BUG] CuTe DSL `CopyUniversalOp` ignores `l1c_evict_priority` again (regression of #3199 since 4.6.0, loads and stores)
items.author: gau-nernst
items.body_excerpt:
### Which component has the problem?

CuTe DSL

### Bug Report

**Describe the bug**
A clear and concise description of what the bug is.

A gmem <-> rmem `cute.copy` through a `CopyUniversalOp` atom built with `l1c_evict_priority=...` emits plain `ld.global` / `st.global` without the `.L1::` qualifier, for both loads and stores and for every priority I tried (`NO_ALLOCATE`, `EVICT_FIRST`, `EVICT_LAST`).

This is the same symptom as #3199 (loads), which was resolved in 4.5.0. It works in 4.5.3 and regressed in 4.6.0. Releases checked: 4.5.3 (good), 4.6.0, 4.6.3, 4.7.0, 4.7.1, 4.8.0 (bad). The PTX operand type also changes from `.u64` to `.b64` at 4.6.0, which suggests the copy now goes through a different lowering path that drops the attribute.

`cute.arch.load` / `cute.arch.store` with `level1_eviction_priority=` still emit the qualifier on 4.8.0, so the problem looks limited to the copy-atom path.

**Steps/Code to reproduce bug**
Follow this guide http://matthewrocklin.com/blog/work/2018/02/28/minimal-bug-reports to craft a minimal bug report. This helps us reproduce the issue you're having and resolve the issue more quickly.

Compile-only (no GPU run needed). It prints the global loads / stores in the generated PTX:

```python
# CuTeDSL MRE: CopyUniversalOp drops l1c_evict_priority (regressed in 4.6.0).
#
# A gmem <-> rmem cute.copy through
#   make_copy_atom(CopyUniversalOp(), ..., l1c_evict_priority=NO_ALLOCATE)
# should emit ld/st.global.L1::no_allocate. 4.5.x does; 4.6.0 - 4.8.0 emit a
# plain ld/st.global for both loads and stores (EVICT_FIRST / EVICT_LAST are
# dropped the same way). cute.arch.load / cute.arch.store with
# level1_eviction_priority still emit the qualifier.
#
# Compile-only; prints the global loads / stores in the generated PTX.
#   python atom_evict_hint.py [NO_ALLOCATE|EVICT_FIRST|EVICT_LAST]
import glob
import importlib.metadata
import os
import re
import sys
import tempfile

DUMP = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="evict_hint_")
os.environ["CUTE_DSL_KEEP_PTX"] = "1"
os.environ["CUTE_DSL_DUMP_DIR"] = DUMP
os.environ["CUTE_DSL_DISABLE_FILE_CACHING"] = "1"

import cutlass.cute as cute  # noqa: E402
from cutlass import Int32  # noqa: E402

PRIO = getattr(
    cute.nvgpu.CacheEvictionPriority, sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "NO_ALLOCATE"
)


def make(hinted):
    @cute.kernel
    def kernel(src: cute.Tensor, dst: cute.Tensor):
        regs = cute.make_rmem_tensor(8, Int32)
        atom = cute.make_copy_atom(
            cute.nvgpu.CopyUniversalOp(), Int32, num_bits_per_copy=256,
            l1c_evict_priority=PRIO,
        )
        plain = cute.make_copy_atom(
            cute.nvgpu.CopyUniversalOp(), Int32, num_bits_per_copy=256
        )
        cute.copy(atom if hinted == "load" else plain, src, regs)
        cute.copy(atom if hinted == "store" else plain, regs, dst)

    @cute.jit
    def run(src: cute.Tensor, dst: cute.Tensor):
        kernel(src, dst).launch(grid=(1, 1, 1), block=(1, 1, 1))

    return run


t = cute.runtime.make_fake_tensor(Int32, (8,), stride=(1,), assumed_align=32)
print("nvidia-cutlass-dsl", importlib.metadata.version("nvidia-cutlass-dsl"), PRIO)
for hinted in ("load", "store"):
    cute.compile(make(hinted), t, t)
    ptx = max(glob.glob(f"{DUMP}/**/*.ptx", recursive=True), key=os.path.getmtime)
    ops = sorted(set(re.findall(r"(?:ld|st)\.global[\w.:]*", open(ptx).read())))
    print(f"  hinted {hinted:5s}: {ops}")
```

Output on 4.8.0 (same on 4.6.0 - 4.7.1):

```
nvidia-cutlass-dsl 4.8.0 CacheEvictionPriority.NO_ALLOCATE
  hinted load : ['ld.global.v4.b64', 'st.global.v4.b64']
  hinted store: ['ld.global.v4.b64', 'st.global.v4.b64']
nvidia-cutlass-dsl 4.8.0 CacheEvictionPriority.EVICT_FIRST
  hinted load : ['ld.global.v4.b64', 'st.global.v4.b64']
  hinted store: ['ld.global.v4.b64', 'st.global.v4.b64']
```

Output on 4.5.3:

```
nvidia-cutlass-dsl 4.5.3 CacheEvictionPriority.NO_ALLOCATE
  hinted load : ['ld.global.L1::no_allocate.v4.u64', 'st.global.v4.u64']
  hinted store: ['ld.global.v4.u64', 'st.global.L1::no_allocate.v4.u64']
nvidia-cutlass-dsl 4.5.3 CacheEvictionPriority.EVICT_FIRST
  hinted load : ['ld.global.L1::evict_first.v4.u64', 'st.global.v4.u64']
  hinted store: ['ld.global.v4.u64', 'st.global.L1::evict_first.v4.u64']
```

**Expected behavior**
A clear and concise description of what you expected to happen.

The hinted direction carries the requested qualifier, as in 4.5.3: `ld.global.L1::no_allocate...` / `st.global.L1::no_allocate...` (SASS `LDG.E.NA` / `STG.E.NA`). If the attribute is no longer supported on this atom, `make_copy_atom` should reject it instead of silently dropping it.

**Environment details (please complete the following information):**
 - Environment location: Bare-metal
 - GPU: NVIDIA GB300 (sm_103a), driver 610.43.02
 - OS: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS (aarch64), Python 3.12.13
 - nvidia-cutlass-dsl: 4.8.0 (also checked 4.5.3, 4.6.0, 4.6.3, 4.7.0, 4.7.1 from PyPI)

**Environment details (please complete the following information):**
 - Environment location: [Bare-metal, Docker, Cloud(specify cloud provider)] 

**Additional context**
Add any other context about the problem here.

comments.author: yunweili3
comments.body:
Reproduced on B200 (sm_100a) with 4.8.0 vs 4.5.3, same output as above.

**Root cause:** the 4.6 update removed the memory attributes from the universal copy atom type itself. `CopyAtomSIMTSyncCopyType.get` now only takes `(value type, bits per copy)` (4.5.3 took `mem order, mem scope, l1 cache eviction priority, invariant` as well), but `CopyUniversalOp._make_trait` kept `**kwargs` and never looks at it, so the attribute is swallowed with no warning. The IR has no slot for it any more, so it cannot be restored on this atom. The specialized ops do carry it: the same MRE with `CopyG2ROp` for the load and `CopyR2GOp` for the store emits `ld.global.L1::no_allocate.v4.b64` / `st.global.L1::no_allocate.v4.b64` on 4.8.0, so that is the supported path.

Side effect of the same regression: the deprecated `cutlass.utils.distributed.ld_bypass` asked `CopyUniversalOp` for a `VOLATILE`/`SYS` load and has been emitting a plain `ld.global` since 4.6.

**PR #3713** makes `CopyUniversalOp` reject these attributes with a `TypeError` that points at the specialized ops (the second behaviour you asked for), and switches `ld_bypass` to `CopyG2ROp`.

items.title: [Feature]: CuTe DSL W4A8 MXFP4 SiTU MoE for Kimi K3
items.author: henrylhtsang
items.body_excerpt:
### Before submitting

- [x] I have searched existing issues and this request has not been filed yet.

### Problem

**tldr**:
* Request for a source visible cute dsl MXFP8×MXFP4 routed MoE backend
* Basically want to be able to inspect and hack around it
* Want feature parity to TensorRT-LLM Gen (e.g. routing and parallelism support, cuda graph)
* performance **doesn't** have to be as good as trtllm gen

## Motivation

We would like an open-source CuTe DSL alternative to the TensorRT-LLM Gen routed mixture-of-experts kernels exposed through FlashInfer. The main benefit is inspectability: we need to be able to read the kernel, profile it, diagnose scheduling or memory problems, make targeted fixes without treating a precompiled kernel as a black box, and hack around it.

The existing TensorRT-LLM Gen implementation should remain the reference for inputs, numerical behavior, and performance. The CuTe DSL implementation can be delivered incrementally rather than reproducing every TensorRT-LLM feature in one pull request.

FlashInfer already has CuTe DSL NVFP4 W4A4 and MXFP8-by-MXFP4 W4A8 MoE paths, but it doesn't have full feature parity. . This request is to make that implementation a practical TensorRT-LLM alternative. For our initial use case, it must support Kimi K3 with:

- NVIDIA B200/B300 as the primary target.
- Native MXFP4 E2M1 weights with UE8M0 group-32 scales.
- W4A8 execution: MXFP4 weights, FP8 E4M3 activations, and BF16 output.
- **SiTU activation. SiLU-and-multiply is not an acceptable substitute.**
- Optimized decode and prefill paths.
- Both 8-way expert parallelism and 8-way MoE tensor parallelism.
- CUDA Graph support without synchronization, allocation, or compilation in the execution path.

The reference entry point is:

```python
from flashinfer.fused_moe import trtllm_fp4_block_scale_routed_moe
```

## Shape and parallelism

| Parameter | Value |
|---|---:|
| Hidden size | 7168 |
| Expert intermediate size | 3072 |
| Routed experts | 896 |
| Experts selected per token | 16 |

Unsharded expert operations:

```text
GEMM1: [tokens_for_expert, 7168] x [7168, 6144]
GEMM2: [tokens_for_expert, 3072] x [3072, 7168]
```

`tokens_for_expert` is ragged and is often zero during decode.

Please support these two rank-local layouts:

| Mode | MoE TP | EP | Local experts | Per-rank intermediate size |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Expert parallel | 1 | 8 | 112 | 3072 |
| MoE tensor parallel | 8 | 1 | 896 | 384 |

Expert-parallel ranks receive global expert identifiers. Rank `r` owns experts `[r * 112, (r + 1) * 112)` and ignores non-local routes. Summing all eight rank-local outputs must reproduce the unsharded result.

MoE-tensor-parallel ranks receive the same inputs and routes, but each rank owns a `3072 / 8 = 384` intermediate-dimension weight shard. Each rank returns a partial `[T, 7168]` BF16 result suitable for a caller-managed all-reduce.

FlashInfer does not need to implement collective communication. Hybrid TP and EP layouts are not required initially.

## Required SiTU behavior

```text
gate_out = beta * tanh(gate / beta) * sigmoid(gate)
up_out   = linear_beta * tanh(up / linear_beta)  if linear_beta is present
           up                                      otherwise
output   = gate_out * up_out
```

Please add an explicit activation value such as `ActivationType.Situ`. `beta` and optional `linear_beta` must be runtime inputs, including per-expert values, rather than hidden compile-time constants.

## Kernel and API requirements

- Accept precomputed global top-k expert identifiers and router weights.
- Accept explicit global expert count, local expert count, and local expert offset.
- Select the parallel mode from explicit metadata, not tensor-shape inference.
- Consume packed MXFP4 weights without converting them to NVFP4.
- Allow a deterministic load-time shuffle without retaining duplicate full-size weights.
- Accept caller-owned output and workspace buffers and expose workspace size before execution.
- Keep workspace bounded for large prefills; fixed-size token slicing is acceptable.
- Run on the caller's CUDA stream without default-stream assumptions.
- Perform no host synchronization, device-to-host metadata reads, allocation, runtime compilation, or serving-time autotuning during execution.
- Capture and replay under CUDA Graphs for every integer token count from `T=1` through `T=16` in both parallel modes.
- Select decode and prefill variants internally using offline tuning data.
- Expose a capability query covering B300, MXFP4, SiTU, dimensions, top-k, parallelism, and CUDA Graph support.
- Fail clearly for unsupported configurations.

A finalized BF16 output is sufficient for the first pull request. A deferred form exposing rank-local GEMM2 rows, router weights, and the assignment-to-row mapping would be useful for fusing finalization with caller-owned collectives.

## Workloads

Decode:

```text
T = 1, 2, 4, 8, 16
```

Prefill:

```text
T = 128, 256, 512, 1024, 2048, 4096
```

If practical, also test `T = 8192, 16384, 32768`.

Test balanced routing, many empty local experts, hot experts, and expert-parallel batches dominated by non-local routes. Report global and per-rank assignment histograms with performance results.


### Requested outcome

- Numerical comparison with TensorRT-LLM Gen at `T = 1, 16, 128, 512, 2048` using identical prepared weights, FP8 inputs, scales, routing, and SiTU parameters.
- Expert-parallel test: summing eight local expert ranges matches the unsharded reference.
- MoE-tensor-parallel test: summing eight intermediate-dimension shards matches the unsharded reference.
- CUDA Graph capture and repeated replay for every integer `T` from 1 through 16 in both modes.
- Correct execution under concurrent CUDA compute and memory-copy streams on B300, including repeated stress testing for intermittent stalls.
- Kernel and runner latency for each listed shape and mode, reported as a ratio to TensorRT-LLM Gen on the same B300.
- Documentatio

items.title: [RLlib] Potential infinite Env Runer sampling loop with non default algorithm parameters
items.author: corentinlger
items.body_excerpt:
### What happened + What you expected to happen

Hi ! While investigating algo configs leading to silently discarded env runners results (https://github.com/ray-project/ray/issues/63302), I ran into a rare but weird case where RLlib training can hang forever without any error. It probably almost never happens, but it still seems a bit weird it's possible, so I'm still posting an issue in case it can help.

The issue: with a synchronous algo on the new API stack (e.g. PPO), if every `sample()` call takes longer than `sample_timeout_s`, each sampling round returns nothing. If `min_sample_timesteps_per_iteration > 0`, the iteration can never reach its minimum, so `train()` loops forever without crashing.

RLlib already warns while this happens and gives a useful advice to fix it, but can still keeps running the training indefinitely.

```
2026-10-01 12:54:33,281 WARNING rollout_ops.py:122 -- No samples returned from remote workers. If you have a slow environment or model, consider increasing the `sample_timeout_s` or decreasing the `rollout_fragment_length` in `AlgorithmConfig.env_runners().
2026-10-01 12:54:35,290 WARNING rollout_ops.py:122 -- No samples returned from remote workers. If you have a slow environment or model, consider increasing the `sample_timeout_s` or decreasing the `rollout_fragment_length` in `AlgorithmConfig.env_runners().
. . .
```

Do you think it would make sense to add a simple safeguard (e.g if no new samples are collected for N consecutive training steps, raise an error and crash the training) ? If so, I can open a quick PR for this (: (but idk if it's worth it as this bug is likely very rare)

### Versions / Dependencies

- Ray 2.58.0
- Python 3.11.13

### Reproduction script

```python
# Toy env whose episodes take ~10s (longer than sample_timeout_s)
class SlowEnv(gym.Env):
    def __init__(self, config=None):
        self.observation_space = spaces.Box(-1.0, 1.0, (2,), np.float32)
        self.action_space = spaces.Discrete(2)
        self._t = 0
        self.n_resets = 0

    def reset(self, *, seed=None, options=None):
        print(f"{self.n_resets = }")
        self.n_resets += 1
        super().reset(seed=seed)
        self._t = 0
        return self.observation_space.sample(), {}

    def step(self, action):
        time.sleep(0.2)          # 50 steps * 0.2s = ~10s per episode
        self._t += 1
        print(f"{self._t = }")
        done = self._t >= 50
        return self.observation_space.sample(), 0.0, done, False, {}

# algo config with low sample timeout + non null min_sample_timesteps_per_iteration
config = (
        PPOConfig()
        .environment(SlowEnv)
        .env_runners(
            num_env_runners=2,
            batch_mode="complete_episodes",
            sample_timeout_s=2.0,          # too low: episodes take ~10s
        )
        .reporting(min_sample_timesteps_per_iteration=100)  # the gate that causes the hang
    )

algo = config.build_algo()
result = algo.train()  # infinite env runner sampling loop
```

### Issue Severity

None

comments.author: lindicaphxag-tech
comments.body:
I put together a draft implementation in #66687 to explore the no-progress safeguard described here. It detects a successful training-step loop that repeatedly makes zero sampling progress while `min_sample_timesteps_per_iteration > 0` and `sample_timeout_s` is finite, and covers both the old counters path and the new lifetime-metrics path.

I have intentionally kept it draft because one design point deserves maintainer input: the current prototype uses `num_consecutive_env_runner_failures_tolerance` as the retry budget, which avoids a new config knob but couples EnvRunner failure tolerance to sampling-timeout/no-progress tolerance. If a separate internal/default budget or dedicated config is preferred, I can adjust before review.

Also happy to defer/close the draft if the original reporter would prefer to implement the fix.

items.title: [Bug]: flashinfer 0.6.18 MLA decode tuning-config cache grows per distinct max KV length; TRT-LLM workaround no-ops
items.author: vsabavat
items.body_excerpt:
### Summary

With `flashinfer-python==0.6.18` (current pin in `requirements.txt`), the MLA decode tuning-config cache in flashinfer grows by one entry per distinct `max_seq_len` value TRT-LLM passes, with no size limit. TRT-LLM's workaround for the related autotuner pathology no longer installs on 0.6.18 and fails without any warning. Host memory grows until every max KV length up to `max_seq_len` has been seen.

### Where

- flashinfer 0.6.18, `flashinfer/mla/_core.py`: `_mla_decode_tuning_config` is wrapped in an unbounded `functools.cache`. Its key includes the block-table width / profile sequence length.
- TRT-LLM, `tensorrt_llm/_torch/attention/backends/fmha/flashinfer_trtllm_gen.py`: the MLA decode call to `trtllm_batch_decode_with_kv_cache_mla` passes `params.max_past_kv_length` as `max_seq_len`. That value changes from batch to batch, so each new max KV length adds a cache entry (~1.6 KB each) in eager MLA decode steps.
- TRT-LLM's `_install_flashinfer_mla_decode_tuning_config_cache` (written for flashinfer 0.6.15) probes the builder with `tensor_initializers=`. On 0.6.18 that raises `TypeError`, the workaround catches it and returns, and nothing is logged.

### Size

The growth is bounded by `max_seq_len`, at one entry per distinct max KV length, per rank:

- 8K context: ~12.7 MiB
- 128K context: ~203 MiB
- 1M context (Kimi K3's 1,048,576): ~1.6 GiB per rank, so ~26 GiB of host memory across a 16-rank job.

Found while soaking Kimi K3 (MLA layers) on 16 x GB200 with host-memory tracing. Other host memory levelled off; this cache was the only per-length growth.

### Possible fixes

1. Pass a stable value for `max_seq_len` (the KV pool / block-table capacity) instead of the per-batch `max_past_kv_length`, so the config key does not change from batch to batch. This needs a check that the kernel only uses it as a bound.
2. Update the workaround for 0.6.18: match the new builder signature, memoize on a bucketed profile sequence length, and log when the workaround cannot install instead of failing without a warning.
3. Upstream in flashinfer: give `_mla_decode_tuning_config` an `lru_cache(maxsize=...)`.

### Environment

TensorRT-LLM main, `flashinfer-python==0.6.18`, PyTorch backend, Kimi K3 (MLA), 16 x GB200 (sm_100).

items.title: [BUG] CuTeDSL >= 4.6 cannot compile NCCL GIN device ops — ptxas rejects the generated PTX (4.5.2 works)
items.author: kiwi3shark
items.body_excerpt:
### Summary

Compiling any NCCL **GIN remote operation** (`Gin.put` / `Gin.signal` from
`nccl4py`'s `nccl.core.device.cute`) with `nvidia-cutlass-dsl >= 4.6` fails in
`ptxas`. The same kernels compile successfully with `nvidia-cutlass-dsl == 4.5.2`.

Two distinct `ptxas` errors appear, and **which one you get is selected by the
NCCL device-bitcode version**, while **whether it fails at all is selected by the
CuTeDSL version**:

| nvidia-cutlass-dsl | nccl4py | nvidia-nccl-cu12 | result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4.5.2 | 0.3.1 | 2.30.7 | **compiles** |
| 4.5.2 | 0.3.1 | 2.31.2 | fails — `Parsing error near '.nvvm'` |
| 4.7.1 | 0.4.1 | 2.30.7 | fails — `Modifier '.volatile' cannot be applied to '.local' space` |
| 4.7.1 | 0.4.1 | 2.31.2 | fails — `Parsing error near '.nvvm'` |

`Gin.wait_counter` / `Gin.wait_signal` / `Gin.read_signal` / `Gin.read_counter`
(the local-poll operations, which do not issue a network operation) compile fine
in **every** combination above. Only the operations that post a remote action fail.

### Defect 1 — unlowered `llvm.nvvm.activemask` leaks into the PTX (NCCL 2.31.2 bitcode)

```
ptxas application ptx input, line 47; fatal : Parsing error near '.nvvm': syntax error
ptxas fatal   : Ptx assembly aborted due to errors
```

The generated PTX contains:

```ptx
.extern .func  (.param .b32 func_retval0) llvm.nvvm.activemask
()
;
```

The `llvm.nvvm.activemask` intrinsic is emitted as an external function
declaration rather than being lowered to `activemask.b32`, and `ptxas` rejects
it because `.` is not legal in a PTX identifier. It is the only leaked intrinsic
in the module (7 references).

This one reproduces on **4.5.2 as well as 4.7.1**, so it looks independent of
the DSL version. Note CuTeDSL's own `cutlass.cute.arch.activemask` is implemented
as inline PTX asm rather than via this intrinsic, so the intrinsic may simply
have no lowering path in the LLVM→NVVM import.

### Defect 2 — `.volatile` applied to `.local` space (NCCL 2.30.7 bitcode)

```
ptxas application ptx input, line 479; error : Modifier '.volatile' cannot be applied to '.local' space
ptxas application ptx input, line 481; error : Modifier '.volatile' cannot be applied to '.local' space
ptxas fatal   : Ptx assembly aborted due to errors
```

This is the interesting one: **the identical bitcode compiles cleanly under
4.5.2 and fails under 4.6.3 / 4.7.1 / 4.8.0.dev0**, which makes it look like a
CuTeDSL codegen regression introduced in 4.6.

### Not architecture specific

Reproduced with `CUTE_DSL_ARCH` set to `sm_90a`, `sm_100a` and `sm_120a` — same
failures. The measurements above were taken on a Blackwell sm_120 (cc 12.0) part,
CUDA driver 580.x.

### Not specific to the `_v2` entry points

`nccl4py` 0.4.1 calls `ncclGinPut_v2` / `ncclGinSignal_v2`, while 0.3.1 calls the
v1 `ncclGinPut`. Declaring the v1 symbols by hand with
`@cute.extern(name="ncclGinPut", source=BitCode(...))` and calling those instead
produces the **same** error for a given NCCL version, so the entry point makes no
difference.

### Reproducer

Single rank, any CUDA GPU; nothing is transferred, both failures are at compile
time.

```bash
pip install 'nvidia-nccl-cu12==2.31.2' 'nccl4py[cu12]==0.4.1' \
            'nvidia-cutlass-dsl==4.7.1' 'cuda-python==12.9.7'

python nvidia_issue_repro.py --case control   # Gin.wait_counter -> COMPILED_OK
python nvidia_issue_repro.py --case v2        # Gin.put / Gin.signal -> fails
python nvidia_issue_repro.py --case v1        # hand-declared v1 externs -> fails
```

Then swap `nvidia-nccl-cu12==2.30.7` to see defect 2 instead of defect 1, and
`nvidia-cutlass-dsl==4.5.2` + `nccl4py[cu12]==0.3.1` for the combination that
works. (0.3.1 and >= 4.6 cannot be mixed: 0.3.1 imports
`cutlass.base_dsl._mlir_helpers.op`, which 4.6.0 removed, and 0.4.1 requires
`~= 4.6`.)

The three cases must be run in **separate processes** — declaring the case `v1`
externs in the same module changes which error the stock path reports.

<details>
<summary>nvidia_issue_repro.py</summary>

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Minimal reproducer: CuTeDSL >= 4.6 cannot compile any NCCL GIN *remote*
operation, while local-poll operations compile fine.

Two independent defects, so the script runs ONE case per process -- declaring
the case B externs in the same module changes the failure reported for case A,
so they must not share a process:

    python nvidia_issue_repro.py --case control   # gin.wait_counter  -> OK
    python nvidia_issue_repro.py --case v2        # gin.put/signal    -> defect 1
    python nvidia_issue_repro.py --case v1        # v1 externs        -> defect 2

Dependencies are three public wheels, nothing else:

    pip install 'nvidia-nccl-cu12==2.30.7' 'nccl4py[cu12]==0.4.1' \
                'nvidia-cutlass-dsl==4.7.1' 'cuda-python==12.9.7'

A single rank on any CUDA GPU is enough; nothing is transferred, both failures
are at compile time.
"""
import argparse

import torch
import cutlass
import cutlass.cute as cute

import cuda.bindings.driver as cuda

import nccl.core as nccl
import nccl.core.device.cute as nccl_cute

items.title: Expert Parallelism (EP) roadmap for SM12x b12x MoE kernel (b12x_fused_moe / B12xMoEWrapper)
items.author: ItamarTerem
items.body_excerpt:
Hi flashinfer team,
We're deploying a large MoE model (384 experts, top_k=8) on 8x RTX PRO 6000 (SM120/Blackwell workstation) using the b12x_fused_moe CuteDSL kernel via TensorRT-LLM's pytorch backend, and have hit the Expert Parallelism restriction:

b12x_fused_moe does not yet support Expert Parallelism
(num_local_experts={X} != num_experts={Y}).
Use a different MoE backend for EP configurations.

This comes from the explicit guard in flashinfer/fused_moe/cute_dsl/b12x_moe.py (both in the free function b12x_fused_moe and in B12xMoEWrapper.__init__), confirmed in flashinfer version 0.6.12.
Context on why this matters for us specifically: without EP, every GPU must retain workspace/routing capacity sized for the full state_E (all 384 experts), even though tensor parallelism already shards each expert's weights across GPUs. This is a meaningful, measured memory cost — in our case, the dynamic workspace's packed_input buffer alone accounts for roughly 7–11GB/GPU across a 60-MoE-layer model, purely from having to size for the worst-case "all experts active" scenario rather than a num_experts/ep_size subset.

What we're asking:

1. Is EP support for the SM12x b12x kernel family (static/dynamic/micro backends) on the roadmap, even at a preliminary stage?
2. Is there a rough timeline or tracking issue we could follow?
3. Are there known architectural blockers specific to SM120 (vs. SM100/SM103, where other kernels like MegaMoE already support EP) that make this a harder problem here?

We also note that vLLM's FlashInferB12xExperts (_supports_parallel_config) explicitly declines to use this backend when EP is requested, for the same underlying reason — so this appears to be a shared, cross-framework limitation rather than something specific to our integration.
Happy to provide more detail on our exact shapes/config if useful. Thanks for your work on this — the b12x kernel has otherwise been the only correctness-verified MoE path we've found for SM120 (CUTLASS produces silently incorrect output on this architecture in our testing).

items.title: [Feature] Check free GPU memory before ModelClaim activation
items.author: jiangxiaobin96
items.body_excerpt:
### 🚀 Feature Description and Motivation

### Problem
Previously, ModelClaim ranked warm Pods using their observed free HBM but did not check whether a Pod had enough memory to start the requested model. A Pod with a cached artifact could be selected even when its free HBM was too low.
If the engine encountered GPU OOM while loading the model, `Activate` could already have returned after spawning the process. The model remained non-routable while the runtime retried it on the same Pod. After the restart budget was exhausted, the runtime and ModelClaim reported a terminal failure; placement did not automatically try another Pod.
```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["Controller selects a warm Pod"] --> B["Runtime Activate spawns the vLLM engine"]
    B --> C["Controller records Activating; route stays disabled"]
    C --> D["Engine loads model into GPU memory"]
    D --> E{"Enough GPU memory?"}
    E -- Yes --> F["Engine ready; ModelClaim becomes Active"]
    E -- No --> G["Engine exits; runtime cleans up and schedules restart"]
    G --> H{"Restart budget remaining?"}
    H -- Yes --> D
    H -- No --> I["Runtime reports failed"]
    I --> J["Controller marks ModelClaim Failed; route remains disabled"]
```

### Solution
Add optional spec.requiredHBMBytesPerGPU, expressed in bytes. When set, placement filters out Pods whose runtime snapshot has no GPU memory observation or whose available HBM is below the requested amount before applying artifact locality and load ranking. For multi-GPU placement, the existing snapshot summary uses the least free HBM across the required GPU group.
Claims that omit the field retain the previous placement behavior. If no Pod has confirmed sufficient capacity, the claim waits for a later reconciliation instead of calling Activate. The API schema, generated clients, tests, and ModelClaim documentation are updated.
This is a placement precheck, not a memory reservation. Concurrent activations and later KV usage can still change available HBM.

### Use Case

No response

### Proposed Solution

_No response_

### Area

Not sure

items.title: [RFC]: Support external routing decisions in the Gateway plugin
items.author: googs1025
items.body_excerpt:
Area: **Gateway**

## Summary

I'd like to get feedback on an optional `external` routing strategy for the AIBrix Gateway plugin.

Today the Gateway ships multiple in-process routing algorithms. They work well for common policies, but users with domain-specific scheduling logic must add that logic to the Gateway codebase. The proposal is to keep discovery, health filtering, admission, accounting, and target validation inside AIBrix while allowing a user-operated HTTP service to select one target from an AIBrix-provided candidate set.

This issue is for design discussion. Before writing code, I'd like to settle the extension point, protocol, security boundary, and failure behavior with the community.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Envoy[Envoy Gateway] <-->|ext_proc| Plugin[AIBrix Gateway Plugin]

    subgraph Gateway[Gateway-owned path]
        Parse[Parse request] --> Filter[Discover and filter candidates]
        Filter --> Router[external Router]
        Router --> Validate[Validate selected pod and port]
        Validate --> Account[Admission and accounting]
    end

    Router <-->|standard HTTP decision protocol| Service[User decision service]
    Router -. failure .-> Fallback[Optional local fallback]
    Account --> Backend[Inference backend]
```

## Motivation

Different deployments may need routing policies that are too environment-specific to become built-in Gateway algorithms, for example:

- Jev-style semantic routing that selects a model tier from request difficulty and confidence;
- proprietary cost, topology, or accelerator-aware placement;
- internal policies based on tenant tier, geography, SLA, cost center, compliance, or experiment cohort;
- routing based on telemetry maintained by another control plane;
- rapid algorithm iteration without rebuilding the Gateway plugin;
- integration with an existing organization-wide scheduling service.

An out-of-process decision service gives users this flexibility, but it also places a network call on the routing hot path. AIBrix therefore needs a narrow and standardized contract with explicit latency, validation, security, and fallback semantics rather than a generic webhook that can mutate arbitrary request state.

The closest related issues I found are:

- #1803, which added `external-filter` label filtering before routing;
- #868, which established the current pluggable `Router`, `RoutingContext`, and `PodList` abstractions;
- #1858, which discussed external load balancing and multi-port data-parallel endpoints.

None of them defines an out-of-process target-selection protocol for the Gateway.

Jev is a current example of why an external decision boundary is useful. Its [model-routing example](https://jev-agent.com/use-cases/llm-model-routing) classifies a request before choosing a model tier, and [LiteLLM's auto-routing documentation](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm-docs/blob/main/docs/proxy/auto_routing.md) includes Jev among its classifier options. That decision happens earlier than AIBrix's current pod router and usually needs request text or a semantic representation. The RFC should distinguish that use case from selecting a replica after the model is already known.

## Proposed Change

### 1. Separate model selection from replica selection

There are two possible extension points:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Request[Inference request] --> ModelPolicy{Optional ModelSelection}
    ModelPolicy -->|Jev or another semantic/business policy| Model[Logical model or tier]
    ModelPolicy -->|Keep requested model| Model
    Model --> Discovery[Gateway model discovery]
    Discovery --> Filters[Candidate filters]
    Filters --> ReplicaPolicy{ReplicaSelection}
    ReplicaPolicy --> Target[Validated pod and port]
```

- `ModelSelection` runs before model discovery and may choose a logical model, tier, or serving pool. Jev-style routing belongs here.
- `ReplicaSelection` runs after model discovery and chooses one pod and port from a Gateway-filtered candidate set. The current `types.Router` interface belongs here.

The concrete v1 protocol below covers `ReplicaSelection`. It must not claim direct Jev support because the hook runs after model selection and excludes raw prompts. The community should decide whether this RFC should also define `ModelSelection`, and whether that hook can receive explicitly opted-in prompt text, an upstream-derived semantic feature, or only trusted policy attributes.

### 2. Add a standalone `external` Router

The first version would implement the existing `types.Router` interface. It would not implement `PodScorer`, so it would be selected as a standalone strategy and would not participate in weighted combinations such as `external:1,prefix-cache:2`.

The existing request path would remain authoritative:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Start[Pods for requested model] --> Routable[Filter non-routable pods]
    Routable --> Labels[Apply external-filter label selector]
    Labels --> Inflight[Apply replica inflight limit]
    Inflight --> Load[Apply normal load-imbalance gate]
    Load --> One{One candidate and one port?}
    One -- Yes --> Fast[Existing direct fast path]
    One -- No --> External[Call external decision service]
    External --> Valid{Valid candidate and port?}
    Valid -- Yes --> Selected[Set target]
    Valid -- No --> Mode{Configured failure mode}
    Mode -- fail-open --> Local[Local fallback, proposed default: least-request]
    Mode -- fail-close --> Error[Routing error / 503]
```

The external service would not be allowed to:

- introduce an arbitrary IP address or URL;
- bypass Gateway health, label, or inflight filtering;
- mutate the inference request or response;
- receive raw prompts, request bodies, authorization headers, or arbitrary client headers;
- replace PD or SLO routing in the initial version.

The request may include a bounded `policyContext` populated from operator-approved sources. This lets an internal service use business attributes such as tenant tier, workload cla
