shortlist.title: [Misc]: CMake Clean-up / Refactor Tasks
shortlist.author: LucasWilkinson
shortlist.body_excerpt:
In an effort to make the CMake more readable, stable and easy to use we have a few tasks we'd like to work on, creating a GitHub issue here to track that progress, some planned changes/investigations:

- [ ] Rename `define_gpu_extension_target`, currently this is used for CPU extensions too so the name is now misleading
- [ ] Add a CI test of local builds, i.e. `pip install -e .`
- [ ]  Warn that PTX builds are not currently supported (post https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/8845), currently if there is a `+PTX` in `TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST` this will be ignored. We should warn when this is the case. Alternatively we can add support for PTX builds although this is generally not desirable since PTX increases the wheel size by quite a bit (PTX is larger than SASS), and we already build for all currently supported arches.
- [ ]  Have vllm-flash-attn use [ExternalProject](https://cmake.org/cmake/help/latest/module/ExternalProject.html) currently vllm-flash-attn uses the parent CMake scope which creates many footguns since it is in a separate repo, using `ExternalProject` will mean that the vllm-flash-attn will be run in a separate CMake scope/process
  - [ ] It might be even better to revert to the FlashMLA approach, where CMake code lives in vllm.
- [ ] Look into removing early returns in CMakeLists.txt (potentially move backends into its own files)
- [ ] Potential build both C++ and CUDA extensions when building for CUDA and using torch dispatcher to dispatch between the two, https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/8424

shortlist.title: [Bug]: Qwen3.8 + DSpark + streaming json_schema can desync XGrammar and emit 250k trailing spaces with HTTP 200
shortlist.author: hr168
shortlist.body_excerpt:
### Your current environment

<details>
<summary>Output collected with the bundled vLLM collect_env.py</summary>

~~~text
OS: Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS (x86_64)
Linux kernel: 6.8.0-137-generic
Python: 3.12.3

vLLM: 0.27.1
vLLM build commit: 6e448d0ea9bf3d88d898b65449ca6dc2aec170ac

PyTorch: 2.13.0+cu130
CUDA used to build PyTorch: 13.0
CUDA runtime: 13.0.88
CUDA image version: 13.0.2

flashinfer-python: 0.6.16.post3
NumPy: 2.2.6
nvidia-cudnn-cu13: 9.20.0.48
nvidia-nccl-cu13: 2.30.7

GPU: NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Workstation Edition
NVIDIA driver: 580.173.02
CUDA architecture reported by collect_env.py includes 12.0
CPU: AMD EPYC 7302 16-Core Processor, 2 sockets, 64 logical CPUs
~~~

The output above is from the container that served the failing request. Very long CPU flag/vulnerability lines were omitted because they are unrelated; full non-secret collect_env.py output can be provided if needed.
</details>

### 🐛 Describe the bug

## Summary

With Qwen3.8-27B NVFP4 served by vLLM 0.27.1 using the Qwen3 reasoning parser, streaming OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions, strict response_format.type=json_schema with a top-level array schema, and DSpark speculative decoding K=7, XGrammar repeatedly logged Failed to advance FSM.

Most calls completed normally, but one call returned HTTP 200 with an incomplete JSON array followed by 249,698 whitespace characters. The vLLM container remained healthy and did not restart.

This looks related to #52852, #53181, #53777 and the accepted-block validation discussed in #52452, but this report adds a separately observed environment and a preserved client-visible failure mode: RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, DSpark K=7, Qwen3 reasoning, explicit JSON Schema array, concurrent streaming, and a roughly 250k-character whitespace tail.

## Related issues / PRs already checked

- #43338 appears to be the same broad structured-output/speculative-decoding family, but focuses on multi-token GPT-OSS reasoning boundaries and reports Qwen3 as its working control.
- #52852 is the closest prior report: Qwen3.8 NVFP4 + streaming + XGrammar with token 271 FSM failures.
- #53181 reports recurrence after the fix referenced when #52852 was closed.
- #53777 reports a similar failure with DFlash2 and json_object.
- #52805 stops XGrammar token batches at grammar termination.
- #52452 validates speculative accepted blocks before commit, explicitly covers reasoning-boundary/grammar-termination invariants, and mentions DSpark K5 qualification.

Please close this as a duplicate if one of those fully covers this path. I am filing it because this is a new DSpark K7 + json_schema top-level array reproduction with a saved malformed response and detailed runtime statistics.

## Effective server launch

The private registry hostname is omitted. The container reports the upstream base tag shown in the environment section. The effective vLLM command was:

~~~bash
vllm serve /model/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4-unsloth --served-model-name /model/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 --language-model-only --reasoning-parser qwen3 --enable-prefix-caching --gpu-memory-utilization 0.55 --port 80 --max-model-len 262144 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-num-seqs 12 --max-num-batched-tokens 24576 --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","model":"/model/Qwen3.8-27B-DSpark-RadixArk","num_speculative_tokens":7,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic"}'
~~~

The startup wrapper maps the draft model architecture name DSparkDraftModel to Qwen3DSparkModel before exec'ing vllm serve. No vLLM Python source files are patched.

## Request shape

The real extraction text is private, so it is redacted below. This is the exact API/options/schema shape, but not yet a deterministic public minimal prompt:

~~~python
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(base_url="http://<vllm-endpoint>/v1", api_key="<redacted>")

response_format = {
    "type": "json_schema",
    "json_schema": {
        "name": "business_database_extraction",
        "strict": True,
        "schema": {
            "type": "array",
            "items": {
                "type": "object",
                "properties": {
                    "field_key": {"type": "string"},
                    "value": {"type": "string"},
                    "chunk_id": {"type": "string"},
                    "confidence": {
                        "type": "number",
                        "minimum": 0,
                        "maximum": 1,
                    },
                },
                "required": [
                    "field_key",
                    "value",
                    "chunk_id",
                    "confidence",
                ],
                "additionalProperties": False,
            },
        },
    },
}

stream = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="/model/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8",
    messages=[
        {"role": "system", "content": "Return only JSON matching the supplied schema."},
        {"role": "user", "content": "<redacted private extraction text>"},
    ],
    max_tokens=25000,
    temperature=0.1,
    top_p=0.95,
    presence_penalty=0.5,
    stream=True,
    stop=[],
    reasoning_effort="medium",
    response_format=response_format,
    extra_body={
        "top_k": 20,
        "repetition_penalty": 1.0,
        "chat_template_kwargs": {
            "enable_thinking": True,
            "preserve_thinking": False,
        },
    },
)
~~~

No tools were requested in these calls. The top-level array schema was accepted by vLLM and normally produced valid arrays in the other calls.

## Reproduction workload

- 10 application-level runs
- concurrency: 2
- each run split the same request into 3 model calls (12, 12 and 5 expected items)
- one downstream repair call after the malformed result
- 31 total model calls in the test
- 30 primary calls used the same private source text and field definitio

shortlist.title: [Bug]: Fake completed replica injection and key spoofing via NotifyOffloadSuccess in Mooncake Store Master
shortlist.author: yyymk
shortlist.body_excerpt:
### Bug Report

### Summary

Mooncake Store Master's `NotifyOffloadSuccess` RPC (unauthenticated, default 0.0.0.0:50051) accepts caller-supplied offload results with no validation. An unauthenticated peer first forges `MountLocalDiskSegment` with its own UUID (satisfying the mounted-segment precondition) and then injects a COMPLETE disk-tier replica pointing at an attacker-chosen endpoint into any existing object, or fabricates metadata for keys that never existed — the master then reports those keys as existing with a completed replica at the attacker's endpoint. Runtime-confirmed on the master binary shipped in the 0.3.13.post1 wheel (latest release); no fix available. Suggested severity: High, CVSS 8.2.

### Details

`MasterService::NotifyOffloadSuccess` (mooncake-store/src/master_service.cpp) processes each caller-supplied (key, StorageObjectMetadata) pair: it clears any in-flight offloading task for the key, then calls `AddReplica(client_id, key, LOCAL_DISK replica{metadata.data_size, metadata.transport_endpoint, ReplicaStatus::COMPLETE})`. Nothing verifies that the caller owns the key, that an offload was ever scheduled, or that the endpoint belongs to the caller.

`AddReplica` widens the effect: when the object has no LOCAL_DISK replica yet (the normal case for a memory-resident object) the forged replica is appended; when the object does not exist at all, the call creates fresh metadata owned by the attacker — so the master's existence oracle and replica lists now answer for keys that were never written.

In 0.3.13 the handler requires `HasMountedLocalDiskSegment(client_id)` when offload is enabled; this is satisfied by first sending one forged `MountLocalDiskSegment(attacker_uuid, enable_offloading=true)`, which is itself unauthenticated. The `client_id` in these RPCs is a self-declared UUID with no binding to the connection.

This is distinct from CVE-2026-96763: that issue forges a segment at mount time to redirect transfers, while this one forges completed object replicas through the offload-completion path — a different method with a different missing check, operating on the object layer rather than the segment layer.

### PoC

Environment: Linux, the 0.3.13.post1 wheel's `mooncake_master` (offload enabled) and a victim client holding a memory-resident object `victim_inject_ky`. The attacker forges coro_rpc frames (20-byte header, magic=21; struct_pack bodies; observed function_ids: MountLocalDiskSegment=673169545, NotifyOffloadSuccess=771250242, GetReplicaList=528413044, ExistKey=2302172937). The 0.3.13 `NotifyOffloadSuccess` body is (UUID, vector<OffloadTaskItem{tenant,key,size}>, vector<StorageObjectMetadata{bucket_id,offset,key_size,data_size,transport_endpoint}>):

```python
call(MountLocalDiskSegment, uuid=ATTACKER_UUID, enable=True)          # ok

call(NotifyOffloadSuccess, uuid=ATTACKER_UUID,
     items=[OffloadTaskItem(tenant="default", key="victim_inject_ky", size=16)],
     metas=[StorageObjectMetadata(bucket_id=1, data_size=16,
                                  endpoint="192.168.105.123:39999")]) # ok
# GetReplicaList("victim_inject_ky") now shows a COMPLETE LOCAL_DISK
# replica owned by the attacker UUID with transport_endpoint
# "192.168.105.123:39999" alongside the victim's memory replica

# key spoof on a key that never existed:
call(GetReplicaList, key="spoofed_key_xyz0")   # OBJECT_NOT_FOUND (-704)
call(NotifyOffloadSuccess, ... key="spoofed_key_xyz0" ...)            # ok
call(ExistKey,     key="spoofed_key_xyz0")     # expected<bool> = true
call(GetReplicaList, key="spoofed_key_xyz0")   # attacker's UUID +
                                               # attacker endpoint, COMPLETE
```

All steps observed verbatim in the captured request/response hex on 0.3.13.post1; the before/after `GetReplicaList` pair for `spoofed_key_xyz0` (-704 → completed replica at the attacker endpoint) is the complete spoof demonstration. Expected secure behavior: offload completion must be bound to an authenticated client and to a task the master scheduled, with the endpoint taken from the registered segment rather than the request.

### Impact

Any network peer that can reach the master RPC port, without credentials, corrupts the persistence-tier metadata plane in two ways. Replica forgery: the master believes an attacker-controlled endpoint holds completed disk replicas of arbitrary victims' keys; any later promotion or disk-tier read that trusts this record can be served from the attacker's endpoint (attacker-supplied cache contents — an integrity attack on the read path; the end-to-end promotion fetch was not demonstrated in this report). Key spoofing: keys that never existed become "existing" with attacker-owned metadata, poisoning the existence oracle that clients and eviction rely on. The call also clears in-flight offloading tasks for arbitrary keys (the disruption variant was not claimed). Integrity of the metadata and read path; availability is not directly affected. Suggested CVSS:3.1 vector AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:H/A:L (8.2), CWE-862. Affected: mooncake-store master <= 0.3.13.post1 (latest release), no patched version yet.
